A 17.5-point spread also caps the second half. Georgia Southern's tackling grade of 55.5 is the risk: it is the one number that lets Houston turn a methodical drive into a short one.

facts: 43.2 grade, weakest unit in this game; 96th in Success Rate defense

The honest projection is his own production adjusted for the matchup, which lands in the 66 to 75 range, and that is still comfortably clear of 52.0.

He is a big-play back: 31.8% breakaway share, 5 explosive runs, a long of 45, 11 avoided tackles and 140 yards after contact on a 77.1 run grade. Tennessee's tackling grade is 62.4, the softest number a defense carries that is otherwise strong at 89.4 coverage, 81.1 pass rush and 73.1 against the run. That split is the reason to attack them on the ground rather than through the passing props in this game.

paras: Tibbs has 15 catches in three games, 5.0 a game, against a line of 3.5. The projection is 5.1. He has run 93 routes and drawn 22 targets, 7.3 a game, which is the volume that makes four catches a normal outcome rather than a good one.

Kansas State's implied team total is 31.0 against a 26.4 league average, the highest on this card, and they are 6.5-point road favorites scoring 45.3 a game. Their passing grade is 62.8, which is the honest argument against a receiving prop here; what the offense does grade well is protection, 81.8 pass block, and that is what keeps a seven-target-a-game route runner on schedule.

Cincinnati's coverage grade is 82.8 and their defense ranks tied 28th in Havoc. That is the argument against, and it is why this is a receptions line rather than a yardage line: volume survives good coverage better than efficiency does. The price is the other consideration, -141.5 on the Over against a line his season rate already clears.
